document.title: Intel® PROSet/Wireless WiFi and Intel® Wireless Bluetooth® Advisory

notes.title: Summary
notes.text: Potential security vulnerabilities in some Intel® PROSet/Wireless WiFi and Intel® Wireless Bluetooth® products may allow denial of service, or escalation of privilege. Intel is releasing firmware and software updates to mitigate these potential vulnerabilities.

notes.title: Recommendation
notes.text:
Intel recommends updating Intel® PROSet/Wireless Wi-Fi software to version 24.50 or later.Updates are available for download at this locations:
exe installer: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/download/19351/812774/windows-10-and-windows-11-wi-fi-drivers-for-intel-wireless-adapters.html
IT admin package: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/download/18231/812775/intel-proset-wireless-software-and-drivers-for-it-admins.html
Intel recommends updating Intel® Wireless Bluetooth® products to version 24.50 or later.Updates are available for download at this location: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/download/18649/intel-wireless-bluetooth-for-windows-10-and-windows-11.html

Intel would like to thank Aobo Wang (CVE-2026-40697), Adonis (CVE-2026-40433), FalconCorruption (CVE-2026-40626) for reporting these issues. 
The other issues were found by Intel employees. Intel, and nearly the entire technology industry, follows a disclosure practice called Coordinated Disclosure, under which a cybersecurity vulnerability is generally publicly disclosed only after mitigations are available.

vulnerabilities.title: Stack-based buffer overflow for some Intel® Wireless Bluetooth® within Ring 0: Kernel may allow a denial of service. Unprivileged software adversary with an unauthenticated user combined with a low complexity attack may enable denial of service. This result may potentially occur via adjacent access when attack requirements are present without special internal knowledge and requires no user interaction. The potential vulnerability may impact the confidentiality (none), integrity (none) and availability (high) of the vulnerable system, resulting in subsequent system confidentiality (none), integrity (none) and availability (none) impacts.

Improper resource shutdown or release for some Intel® PROSet/Wireless Wi-Fi Software for Windows within Ring 3: User Applications may allow a denial of service. Unprivileged software adversary with an authenticated user combined with a low complexity attack may enable denial of service. This result may potentially occur via local access when attack requirements are not present without special internal knowledge and requires no user interaction. The potential vulnerability may impact the confidentiality (none), integrity (none) and availability (high) of the vulnerable system, resulting in subsequent system confidentiality (none), integrity (none) and availability (none) impacts.

Unprivileged software adversary with an authenticated user combined with a high complexity attack may enable escalation of privilege. This result may potentially occur via local access when attack requirements are present without special internal knowledge and requires active user interaction. The potential vulnerability may impact the confidentiality (high), integrity (high) and availability (high) of the vulnerable system, resulting in subsequent system confidentiality (none), integrity (none) and availability (none) impacts.

The potential vulnerability may impact the confidentiality (none), integrity (high) and availability (high) of the vulnerable system, resulting in subsequent system confidentiality (none), integrity (high) and availability (high) impacts.
